status: draft-v4 (internal assistive; a human reviewer is the final authority)

defaults.perspective_preference: One-way (unilateral) with Amperesand Inc as the sole Disclosing Party and the service provider as Receiving Party; this favorable one-sidedness is INTENTIONAL because Amperesand discloses product/engineering/manufacturing IP downstream to a vendor that discloses little or nothing back.
defaults.forum: AAA Commercial Arbitration Rules, single arbitrator, seat in Nevada, USA, conducted in English; court carve-out permitting either party (in practice the Disclosing Party / Amperesand) to seek injunctive/equitable relief in any court of competent jurisdiction.
defaults.term_standard: Agreement term: one (1) year from the Effective Date, terminable earlier by either Party on written notice (template Clause 8).
defaults.survival_standard: Template Clause 8 states confidentiality rights/obligations survive any termination or expiration but sets NO finite period (drafting defect). Adopted internal default: 5 years per disclosure for ordinary Confidential Information + an uncapped trade-secret tail (as long as it remains a trade secret under DTSA / applicable state UTSA), measured from each disclosure (rolling), with a 3-year pre-authorized fallback. Pending counsel refinement.
required_carveouts: prior_possession (already in the Receiving Party's possession or known to it before disclosure)
public_domain (is or comes into the public domain through no fault or breach by the Receiving Party or its Representatives)
third_party (received from a third party not under any obligation of confidentiality)
independent_development (independently developed by the Receiving Party without regard or reference to the Confidential Information)
written_authorization (approved for release or use by written authorization of the Disclosing Party)
counsel_must_confirm: ADOPTED (pending counsel): the uNDA Clause 4 -> Clause 8 cross-reference sets no finite survival period (template defect). Adopted default: 5yr per-disclosure ordinary CI + uncapped trade-secret tail, 3yr fallback.
ADOPTED (pending counsel): an uncapped/perpetual trade-secret carve-out is the standard survival default; confirm approved drafting language.

RESOLVED: US/Amperesand Inc forum = AAA Commercial Arbitration Rules, single arbitrator, seat Nevada (template Clause 16, template-true). Delaware-seated executed deals are drift, demoted to fallback.
RESOLVED: compelled disclosure is a separate Required-Disclosure-with-notice clause (template Clause 3), not the 5th definitional exclusion (which is written-authorization).
RESOLVED: injunctive/equitable-relief court carve-out is the standard default alongside arbitration (template Clause 12 + Clause 16).

STANDING (per-deal judgment): on the rare occasion a service-provider counterparty puts forward its own paper or amends Amperesand's, run the fallback ladders below; default expectation is that this counterparty type signs Amperesand paper verbatim.

STANDING (service-provider specific): if the engagement will generate deliverables/work product (designs, drawings, firmware, tooling, samples, test reports), confirm IP ownership and work-product assignment in the definitive services/MSA agreement — the NDA is NOT the IP-vesting instrument and must not be expanded to assign Amperesand's IP to the vendor.

STANDING: foreign service-provider counterparties (e.g., an overseas contract manufacturer) have signed the Delaware/AAA-Nevada template verbatim; confirm enforceability and any export-control exposure per deal rather than conceding governing law/forum.

positions.title: Definition of Confidential Information
positions.standard_position: Confidential Information is defined broadly as any and all information relating to the Purpose, disclosed in writing or orally by or on behalf of the Disclosing Party (Amperesand) to the Receiving Party (the service provider) or to an authorized third party acting on its behalf, which is marked or communicated as confidential, PLUS a catch-all sweeping in unmarked information that is reasonably apparent to someone familiar with the subject area as the type typically treated as confidential (or that the Receiving Party has reason to believe may be confidential). It expressly covers: the existence/terms of the agreement and the negotiations; Amperesand's business, affairs, customers, suppliers, plans and market opportunities (and those of its Affiliates and contemplated subsidiaries); its IP, operations, processes, product information, know-how, technical information, designs, trade secrets and software (and those of its Affiliates / future portfolio companies); derived data/analyses; shared personal data; and third-party confidential information held by Amperesand. No oral-to-writing confirmation deadline and no marking requirement to qualify. (Template Clause 1.)
walk_away_triggers: Adding a marking/legending requirement or an oral-to-writing memorialization deadline (e.g., must confirm in writing within 15-30 days) as a precondition to protection — strips protection from Amperesand's unmarked engineering/manufacturing disclosures, which are the bulk of what a service provider receives.

Narrowing the definition so it only protects information the vendor agrees to receive or only formally 'delivered' deliverables, leaving Amperesand's broader shared information (financials, roadmaps, customer/supplier identities, designs shown on-site) outside scope.

A reciprocal/mutual expansion that auto-deems the vendor's own samples, yield data, tooling, process know-how or pre-production articles as that vendor's Confidential Information regardless of marking — converts a one-way protective NDA into a two-way instrument that binds Amperesand as receiver of low-value vendor data.
Cloud/third-party-processing acknowledgment inserted into the definition that can be read as Amperesand accepting reduced confidentiality controls for cloud-stored CI it discloses.
Burden-of-proof-on-the-discloser language requiring Amperesand to prove information qualifies as confidential, combined with deletion of the 'reasonably apparent' catch-all.

Embedding foreign (e.g., non-US data-protection or companies-act) statutory definitions into this Delaware-governed US-to-US service-provider agreement, creating jurisdictional ambiguity — clean out before signing.
acceptable_fallbacks: Adding a confidentiality legend/marking PRACTICE for documents while preserving protection for oral/visual disclosures and retaining the 'reasonably apparent / reason to believe' catch-all (no hard memorialization deadline).
A symmetric mutual definition where the engagement genuinely involves two-way disclosure (e.g., the vendor shares proprietary process IP), provided Amperesand's broad scope is preserved unchanged.
Excluding the existence/terms-of-agreement limb only where the vendor must disclose the relationship to its own auditors/regulators, replaced by a need-to-know permitted-disclosure right.

positions.title: Purpose Limitation
positions.standard_position: Confidential Information may be used by the service provider solely for the single, narrowly defined 'Purpose' stated in the recitals — evaluating and (if engaged) performing the specific services engagement for which Amperesand is considering the vendor (e.g., circuit board assembly, engineering/design and thermal cooling, contract manufacturing, valve design and manufacturing support, drawing) — and for no other purpose. (Template recitals + Clause 4.)
walk_away_triggers: Vendor-side purpose expansion permitting use of Amperesand's CI for the vendor's other customers, its own product development, or to improve its general processes/tooling beyond the specific engagement — enables Amperesand's designs to bleed into the vendor's other work.

Anti-reverse-engineering or 'design-around' prohibition embedded in the purpose clause drafted broadly enough to constrain Amperesand's own legitimate independent engineering (Amperesand should never be use-restricted on its own paper as discloser; resist if reciprocated).

Leaving the Purpose as an unfilled bracketed placeholder ('[describe services]', '[Drawing]') in the executed copy — observed in executed paper where a bracketed Purpose was left unfilled — finalize to a single complete Purpose before signing to avoid scope ambiguity.

Open-ended catch-all extending permitted use to 'business activities arising from the relationship' or 'other purposes as the parties may agree,' converting an evaluation/engagement NDA into a standing operational-use license without a definitive services agreement.
acceptable_fallbacks: Describing the Purpose to cover both evaluation AND performance of the named services (so a single NDA spans the engagement) provided it stays tied to the specific named services.

A narrow, mutual reverse-engineering restriction limited to genuine misappropriation of the specific disclosed CI, with an express carve-in for Amperesand's pre-existing and independently developed work.

positions.title: Exclusions from Confidential Information
positions.standard_position: Five standard exclusions, with the Receiving Party (vendor) bearing them: (a) prior possession/knowledge before disclosure; (b) public domain through no fault or breach by the Receiving Party or its Representatives; (c) third-party receipt with no confidentiality obligation; (d) independent development without regard or reference to the CI; (e) approved for release or use by written authorization of the Disclosing Party. Compelled disclosure is handled separately as Required Disclosure (Clause 3), NOT as an exclusion. (Template Clause 2.)
walk_away_triggers: Broadening the independent-development carve-out so the vendor can claim anything it later builds was 'independently developed,' or dropping the 'without regard or reference to the Confidential Information' qualifier — lets a manufacturing/design vendor launder Amperesand's designs into 'its own' work.
A public-domain carve-out drafted as 'whatever later becomes public' without the 'through no fault or breach by the Receiving Party' qualifier, rewarding the vendor's own leaks.
Adding exclusions beyond the five standard ones (e.g., 'information of a general nature,' 'residuals,' 'information retained in memory') that erode protection of Amperesand's disclosed CI.
Recasting compelled disclosure as a 6th blanket exclusion (removing the notice/minimization/confidential-treatment obligations of the separate Required Disclosure clause).
acceptable_fallbacks: Tightening the third-party carve-out to require the third party be 'not known by the Receiving Party to be under' a confidentiality obligation (knowledge qualifier) — acceptable as it favors Amperesand as discloser.
Express statement that the burden of proving an exclusion rests on the Receiving Party (favors Amperesand).

positions.title: Confidentiality Obligations of the Receiving Party
positions.standard_position: The service provider must hold Amperesand's CI in strict confidence and not disclose it to any third party without Amperesand's prior written approval; use it for no purpose other than the Purpose; apply at least the same degree of precaution it uses for its own CI of like importance but in no event less than reasonable care; limit access to its Representatives (directors, officers, employees, consultants, advisers) strictly on a need-to-know basis; remain responsible for any Representative breach and take all reasonable measures (including court proceedings) to restrain unauthorized disclosure; not copy or record CI except as strictly necessary for the Purpose (such copies being Amperesand's property); and immediately notify Amperesand of any loss or unauthorized disclosure. (Template Clause 4.)
walk_away_triggers: Diluting the care standard below reasonable care, or making the obligation expire with the agreement term rather than surviving up to the Clause 8 survival period.

Carving the vendor's affiliates, sister factories, sub-tier suppliers or other customers into the permitted-disclosee universe without a direct need-to-know/Purpose tether and without the vendor remaining responsible for their breaches — a real manufacturing-vendor risk (work pushed to sub-tier shops).
Removing the vendor's responsibility for its Representatives' breaches, or converting it from full responsibility to a mere 'will inform its Representatives of the obligations' standard.
Deleting the 'copies are Disclosing Party's property' / 'not copy except as strictly necessary' limb so the vendor may freely reproduce Amperesand's drawings and designs.

On counterparty paper where roles flip and Amperesand becomes the receiver: a mandatory affirmative obligation to litigate against its own Representatives at its own cost, a requirement that each Representative individually sign undertakings before access, or an AI-training prohibition / one-sided cybersecurity-audit-and-remediation-at-Amperesand's-expense regime bolted on — push back or reciprocate.
acceptable_fallbacks: Permitting the vendor to share with named sub-tier suppliers necessary to perform the services, provided each is bound by written confidentiality terms at least as protective and the vendor remains fully responsible for them.
A 'commercially reasonable' notification window (e.g., within 2-3 business days) in place of 'immediately' for loss/unauthorized-disclosure notice.
Accepting vicarious liability for Representatives without the mandated 'court proceedings' affirmative-enforcement language.

positions.title: Permitted Disclosures (Representatives and Compelled)
positions.standard_position: The service provider may disclose Amperesand's CI (a) to its Representatives on a need-to-know basis for the Purpose, remaining responsible for their compliance; and (b) where compelled by a valid court order or governmental/regulatory authority with jurisdiction, provided it gives Amperesand reasonable prior written notice (to the extent legally permitted), discloses only the minimum required, uses reasonable efforts to obtain confidential treatment, and gives prompt post-hoc notice if advance notice was impossible. (Template Clauses 3 and 4.)
walk_away_triggers: Granting the vendor a standing right to disclose to its affiliates, sister plants, financing sources or other customers without Amperesand's consent and without a compulsion trigger.
Removing the prior-notice / minimization / confidential-treatment obligations from the compelled-disclosure mechanism, or removing the compelled-disclosure clause entirely.
A standing third-party (e.g., customer or regulator) inspection or pass-through right not tied to actual legal compulsion.
Long fixed advance-notice periods (e.g., 30 days) for compelled disclosure that cannot be met under urgent orders.
acceptable_fallbacks: Adding the vendor's outside legal/accounting advisors to the need-to-know Representative set, provided they are bound by professional or contractual confidentiality duties.
A 'to the extent legally permitted' notice standard (rather than absolute notice) on compelled disclosure — already the template position and acceptable.

positions.title: Required (Compelled) Disclosure
positions.standard_position: If the service provider (or its Representative) is obligated or requested to disclose Amperesand's CI under a valid court order or governmental/regulatory authority with jurisdiction, it shall (i) give Amperesand reasonable prior written notice, (ii) disclose only the CI required by the order/authority, and (iii) use reasonable efforts to ensure the CI is accorded confidential treatment; if it cannot notify Amperesand beforehand, it shall, to the extent permitted by law, inform Amperesand of the full circumstances and the information disclosed as soon as reasonably practicable. (Template Clause 3.)
walk_away_triggers: Deletion of the prior-written-notice obligation, the minimization ('only such CI required') obligation, or the confidential-treatment-efforts obligation.

Shifting onto Amperesand (as discloser) the cost or sole burden of resisting/limiting the vendor's compelled disclosure as a baseline term, or requiring Amperesand to take 'all steps the vendor may require' to fight the order.
Treating compelled disclosure as an outright exclusion that ends all obligations rather than a narrow, notice-bound permitted disclosure.
acceptable_fallbacks: Replacing 'reasonable prior written notice' with 'prompt notice to the extent legally permitted' where a protective order or gag applies.
Permitting disclosure to a regulator under a routine, recurring filing obligation provided confidential-treatment efforts and post-hoc notice are preserved.

positions.title: Term of the Agreement
positions.standard_position: The Agreement commences on the Effective Date and expires one (1) year from the Effective Date, subject to earlier termination by either Party on written notice. Each Party's rights and obligations survive any termination or expiration. (Template Clause 8.)
walk_away_triggers: Vendor-imposed perpetual/evergreen term with no fixed expiry that survives indefinitely absent affirmative notice (resist; if accepted, retain a short termination-for-convenience right).
Removing the bilateral early-termination-on-notice right, locking Amperesand into the full term with no exit.
A term tied to or floored by an underlying supply/MSA agreement (e.g., 5-7 year minimums) with no independent NDA termination right.
Internal word/numeral contradiction in the term figure (spelled-out number disagreeing with the parenthetical) — correct before signature.
acceptable_fallbacks: A 2-3 year agreement term matched to the expected length of the services engagement, provided the bilateral termination-on-notice right is retained.
A term that auto-renews annually but remains terminable on notice by either party.

positions.title: Survival of Confidentiality Obligations
positions.standard_position: Confidentiality rights and obligations survive any termination or expiration of the Agreement (template Clause 8 'will survive'), but the template sets NO finite survival period (drafting defect). Adopted internal default: ordinary Confidential Information protected for 5 years per disclosure (3-year pre-authorized fallback); trade secrets protected for as long as they remain trade secrets under DTSA / applicable state UTSA (uncapped); measured from the date of each disclosure (rolling, per-item), NOT the Effective Date. Pending counsel refinement.
walk_away_triggers: No post-termination survival at all, or confidentiality co-terminous with the (1-year) agreement term — leaves Amperesand's disclosed designs/CI unprotected once the short term ends.
A finite survival cap on trade secrets (e.g., 'all obligations end after N years' with no trade-secret tail) when Amperesand is disclosing trade-secret-grade manufacturing/design IP.
Survival anchored to the Effective Date with a period equal to or shorter than the agreement term, producing zero or near-zero effective post-expiry tail.
Internally contradictory survival drafting a court could read as expiring with the agreement, or a word/numeral mismatch — fix before signing.
acceptable_fallbacks: 3 years per disclosure for ordinary CI (the pre-authorized fallback) PLUS the uncapped trade-secret tail.
Survival re-anchored to termination/expiry (rather than the Effective Date) to lengthen the post-expiry tail, with the trade-secret tail preserved.

positions.title: Return or Destruction of Confidential Information
positions.standard_position: On Amperesand's written request or upon expiration/termination, the service provider must within fourteen (14) days return or destroy all documents and tangible materials representing Amperesand's CI and all copies, except it may retain one (1) copy (including electronic records from automatic archiving/back-up) solely to perform surviving obligations and as required by law, court, regulatory authority, or its internal audit/compliance procedures; the Agreement continues to apply to any retained copy. (Template Clause 7.)
walk_away_triggers: Retention satisfied by reference to the vendor's own record-retention or document-governance policy (rather than a specific legal requirement), letting it keep Amperesand's CI as long as its policies allow — renders the destroy obligation illusory.
Open-ended/indefinite retention of backup/archival copies with no sunset and no continuing confidentiality tail on retained copies.
A broad carve-out letting the vendor retain derivative work product (notes, analyses, process records) derived from Amperesand's CI.
Return-only with no destruction option and no certification mechanism, or loss of Amperesand's right to demand return on demand at any time.
acceptable_fallbacks: A modestly longer return/destruction window (e.g., 30 days) to accommodate the vendor's IT/back-up cycle.
A written certification of destruction in lieu of physical return for electronically stored CI.
Retention of the single archival copy under the template's narrow legal/compliance purpose, with the Agreement continuing to govern it (already the template position).

positions.title: No Transfer of Rights, Title, or Interest
positions.standard_position: Amperesand retains all right, title and interest in its Confidential Information (including copies and extracts) and grants no licenses or rights except those expressly set out; nothing grants a license to, or waives any rights in, any patents, copyrights, trademarks or mask works belonging to Amperesand. (Template Clause 10.)
walk_away_triggers: Any IP-assignment, vesting, or work-for-hire obligation requiring Amperesand to assign or transfer ownership of IP, inventions, designs or 'derivatives of Confidential Information' to the vendor — an NDA must not become an IP-transfer instrument; defer all work-product/deliverable IP to the definitive services/MSA.
A clause purporting to grant the vendor a license to Amperesand's IP, or deeming disclosure an implied license/waiver of Amperesand's patents/copyrights/trademarks/mask works.

A patent-filing prohibition barring Amperesand from filing on information exchanged, or 'derived directly or indirectly / in the course of interaction' IP-capture language that sweeps in Amperesand's own innovations.
A clause vesting ownership of vendor-created tooling, fixtures or process improvements (made using Amperesand's designs) in the vendor with no license back to Amperesand.
acceptable_fallbacks: A neutral statement that each party retains its own pre-existing IP (acceptable since Amperesand is the primary discloser; ensure vendor improvements built on Amperesand's CI do not vest solely in the vendor).
Deferring all work-product/deliverable ownership expressly to the definitive services agreement (preferred), with the NDA silent on vesting.

positions.title: No Warranty / No Other Obligations (AS-IS)
positions.standard_position: Nothing compels Amperesand to supply any particular CI (it may decline at its discretion) or to enter into any transaction; no partnership, joint venture or agency is created; either party may terminate discussions at any time. By implication the CI is provided without representation or warranty as to accuracy/completeness and Amperesand bears no liability for the vendor's use or reliance. (Template Clause 6; consider adding an express AS-IS disclaimer.)
walk_away_triggers: An affirmative warranty extracted from Amperesand (accuracy, completeness, non-infringement, fitness, performance of its CI) beyond the narrow right to disclose.

A consequential/indirect/punitive damages waiver or liability cap bundled in that would limit Amperesand's recovery when the vendor misuses or improperly discloses its CI — if it must remain, carve out confidentiality breaches and IP misappropriation.
A no-warranty clause coupled with an indemnity by Amperesand for the vendor's use of/reliance on disclosed information (indemnity in an NDA is dealbreaker-class).
acceptable_fallbacks: A mutual AS-IS / no-reliance disclaimer (acceptable and protective of Amperesand as discloser).
A mutual limitation excluding consequential damages provided confidentiality breaches and IP misappropriation are expressly carved out of the limitation.

positions.title: Remedies / Injunctive Relief
positions.standard_position: Each Party acknowledges monetary damages alone may be insufficient for a breach and agrees Amperesand (as Disclosing Party) may seek specific performance or injunctive relief from any court in any jurisdiction, in addition to all other remedies available — a non-exclusive remedy, with no bond requirement and no cap on or waiver of monetary damages. (Template Clause 12.)
walk_away_triggers: Deleting the injunctive-relief / irreparable-harm acknowledgment, leaving Amperesand without an express equitable remedy for the vendor's misuse of its designs.
Requiring Amperesand to post a bond, or imposing a fixed/nominal bond cap, as a precondition to injunctive relief.
Narrowing injunctive relief to IP-infringement only, excluding ordinary confidentiality breaches.
Prevailing-party attorneys'-fee shifting bolted on (not in Amperesand's template), which asymmetrically deters enforcement.
On flipped/counterparty paper: a blanket pre-emptive waiver requiring Amperesand (as recipient) to not oppose injunctive relief.
acceptable_fallbacks: Making the injunctive-relief right mutual (either party as discloser) — acceptable and consistent with the template's reciprocal-acknowledgment framing.
Specifying that injunctive relief is sought in a court of competent jurisdiction notwithstanding the arbitration clause (clarifies the carve-out).

positions.title: Governing Law and Dispute Resolution
positions.standard_position: Governed by the laws of the State of Delaware. Disputes are referred to arbitration by the American Arbitration Association under its Commercial Arbitration Rules, single arbitrator, seat in Nevada, USA. A court carve-out for injunctive/equitable relief applies via the remedies clause. (Template Clause 16 + Clause 12.)
walk_away_triggers: Replacing Delaware law / AAA-Nevada arbitration with the vendor's home-jurisdiction law and forum — especially a foreign vendor's home seat (e.g., an overseas contract manufacturer's local courts/arbitration institution, or other foreign institutional seats) giving the counterparty home-court advantage.
Specifying governing law but no forum/dispute mechanism, or a forum but no governing law.
An internally contradictory forum clause naming two incompatible institutions or seats in one provision (risk of a void clause).
Litigation in the vendor's home courts with prevailing-party fee-shifting to the vendor.
Ambiguous choice-of-law ('internal laws of the United States') without a named state, or embedding foreign statutory references in this Delaware-governed agreement.
acceptable_fallbacks: AAA arbitration seated in Delaware (rather than Nevada) — observed drift in some executed US deals; acceptable fallback, not the standard.
A neutral US state's law and a neutral seat (e.g., New York) where a foreign vendor resists Delaware/Nevada, provided arbitration (not the vendor's home courts) is retained.
Court litigation in a neutral US federal/state forum in lieu of arbitration only where a per-deal judgment supports it.

positions.title: Assignment
positions.standard_position: Neither Party may assign rights or delegate obligations without the other's prior written consent, except that (i) Amperesand (Disclosing Party) may assign to a person/entity acquiring substantially all its assets directly or by operation of law, and (ii) Amperesand may assign to any Affiliate. Any purported assignment in violation is null and void; assignment does not relieve the assignor of its obligations; the Agreement binds successors and permitted assigns only. (Template Clause 15.)
walk_away_triggers: Granting the vendor a free right to assign or delegate (including to affiliates, sub-tier suppliers, or on its own M&A/change of control) without Amperesand's consent — transfers access to Amperesand's CI to an unknown third party.
A 'binding on successors and assigns' clause with no consent requirement, allowing automatic assignment by either side.
Making the assignment restriction one-sided against Amperesand while leaving the vendor free to assign (the template's intentional one-sidedness runs the OTHER way — in Amperesand's favor).
Deleting Amperesand's Affiliate / asset-sale assignment carve-outs.
Removing the assignment clause entirely, defaulting to permissive local-law assignment rules.
acceptable_fallbacks: Permitting the vendor to assign in connection with a sale of all its assets/business to a non-competitor of Amperesand, with prior written notice and the assignee bound by the NDA.
Mutualizing the affiliate/asset-sale carve-outs so both parties have symmetric M&A assignment rights, provided assignment to an Amperesand competitor still requires consent.

positions.title: Residuals (No Residuals Clause)
positions.standard_position: Amperesand's template contains NO residuals clause and no competitive-use carve-out; the vendor must keep CI confidential and use it solely for the Purpose, with no right to use memory-retained 'residuals' or to apply Amperesand's CI to other customers, its own products, or competing development.
walk_away_triggers: A residuals clause permitting the vendor to use information retained in the unaided memory of its personnel for any purpose — a serious leakage vector for a manufacturing/design vendor that works for Amperesand's competitors.
A competitive-use or 'general process improvement' carve-out letting the vendor apply Amperesand's CI to develop or improve products/tooling for other customers.
Any residuals/employee-reassignment clause lacking an express prohibition on direct use of Amperesand's CI.
acceptable_fallbacks: If a vendor insists, a narrowly cabined residuals concept limited to genuinely unaided memory AND expressly excluding any use that competes with Amperesand or applies its specific designs/trade secrets — documented as a counterparty-paper fallback only, never Amperesand-standard.
Reject residuals entirely (preferred); offer instead a clean need-to-know Representative model.

positions.title: Non-Solicitation (Prohibited)
positions.standard_position: Amperesand's template contains NO standalone non-solicitation covenant; an NDA is a confidentiality instrument, not a trade-restraint vehicle. An inserted non-solicit is treated as prohibited, high-severity, and walk-away-class (a narrow, use-tethered, mutual non-solicit may be entertained only as a documented counterparty-paper fallback).
walk_away_triggers: Any standalone non-solicitation covenant untethered from use of Confidential Information.
A non-solicit binding only Amperesand (one-way against the discloser), or exceeding 12 months / perpetual.
A non-solicit lacking a general-advertising / non-targeted-recruiting carve-out.
A customer/supplier non-solicit broad enough to restrain Amperesand's ordinary business (de facto non-compete).
Liquidated damages or indemnity tied to a non-solicit breach.
acceptable_fallbacks: A narrow, mutual, time-limited (<=12 months) no-poach of employees who worked directly on the engagement, with a public-advertising carve-out — documented as a counterparty-paper fallback only.
Deletion (preferred).

positions.title: Non-Competition (Prohibited)
positions.standard_position: Amperesand's template contains NO non-competition clause; an NDA should remain a confidentiality instrument only. Preferred position: no non-compete, no non-compete-taint restriction, and no non-compete waiver in either direction.
walk_away_triggers: Any non-compete or 'residual contamination'/taint restriction barring Amperesand personnel exposed to vendor information from working on competing technology — a de facto non-compete on Amperesand's engineering teams.
A broad 'competes' definition tied to a personnel-segregation/taint obligation that could sterilize Amperesand's R&D roadmap.
A non-compete waiver extracted from Amperesand acknowledging the vendor may serve Amperesand's competitors, with no reciprocal confidentiality/use safeguards.
Any actual restraint on Amperesand competing, embedded in the NDA.
acceptable_fallbacks: Deletion (preferred).

If a vendor seeks acknowledgment that it serves other customers, a narrow statement that the vendor may work for others provided it does not use or disclose Amperesand's CI and maintains information barriers — no taint/segregation obligation on Amperesand.

positions.title: Indemnification (Prohibited)
positions.standard_position: Amperesand's standard NDA contains NO indemnification, hold-harmless, or fee-shifting provision; confidentiality breaches are remedied through general-law damages and equitable relief. Preferred position: strike any indemnity or attorneys'-fees clause.
walk_away_triggers: An indemnity running against Amperesand (as discloser) for the vendor's use of/reliance on disclosed information, or any uncapped one-way indemnity.
Legal costs recoverable on a solicitor-client / 'indemnity basis' rather than reasonable party-and-party costs.
Indemnity/liability extending to 'attempted or threatened' disclosure and to a broad indemnitee list (affiliates, agents, advisors, officers, directors).
Any non-mutual fee-shifting or indemnity running only in the vendor's favor.
Indemnity lacking carve-outs aligned to the confidentiality exclusions and compelled disclosure.
acceptable_fallbacks: If unavoidable, a mutual indemnity capped and excluding indirect/consequential loss, limited to third-party claims arising from a confidentiality breach — documented as a counterparty-paper fallback only.
Deletion (preferred).

positions.title: Notices, Waiver, Severability, Counterparts, E-Signature
positions.standard_position: Notices effective on delivery by hand, email, or certified/registered mail to the specified addresses (Amperesand's designated notice contacts). Clean boilerplate: no-waiver (Clause 11), severability (Clause 13), and counterparts/PDF-or-e-signature execution (Clause 17) recognizing electronic-signature platforms as original signatures. (Template Clauses 9, 11, 13, 17.)
walk_away_triggers: Leaving counterparty notice details as blank/placeholder fields ('[name]', '[address]', '[insert]') in an executed agreement — observed across executed paper where bracketed notice fields were left unfilled — never sign with placeholder notice details, as it undermines valid service.
Embedding foreign (non-US) statutory references (data-protection, companies-act, or electronic-transactions statutes) in this Delaware/US-governed agreement.
An attorneys'-fee / prevailing-party fee-shifting clause inserted (not in Amperesand's standard).
A unilateral right to transfer the NDA and all received CI to a government agency without consent/notice.

An export-control clause making Amperesand liable for the vendor's unauthorized export, or conditioning disclosure on the vendor's government permits, rather than each party bearing its own compliance.
acceptable_fallbacks: Adding the US e-signature statutory reference (ESIGN + Delaware UETA) — an improvement, not a deviation.
A mutual, each-party-bears-its-own-compliance export-control acknowledgment (relevant for foreign service providers).
Updated/completed counterparty notice details (required before signature).

positions.title: Entire Agreement and Amendments
positions.standard_position: The Agreement is the final, complete and exclusive agreement on its subject matter, superseding and merging all prior discussions; no modification or amendment is effective unless in writing and signed by authorized representatives of both Parties. (Template Clause 14.)
walk_away_triggers: Deleting the written-signed-amendment requirement (allowing oral or course-of-dealing modification).
An integration clause drafted to supersede or subordinate a future definitive services/MSA agreement, or to merge away Amperesand's separately negotiated IP/work-product terms.
Incorporating the vendor's standard terms or purchase-order terms by reference.
acceptable_fallbacks: A carve-out clarifying that the NDA does not supersede any concurrent or future definitive services/MSA agreement between the parties (preferred where an engagement is contemplated).
Standard mutual integration language.

positions.title: Work Product / Deliverables (Service-Provider-Specific; Not in the NDA)
positions.standard_position: Amperesand's NDA template contains NO work-product, deliverables, or IP-assignment clause, and intentionally so: the NDA is a confidentiality instrument and ownership of deliverables, designs, drawings, firmware, tooling, fixtures, and process improvements generated by the service provider must be allocated in the definitive services/MSA agreement, not the NDA. Amperesand's default position in that downstream agreement is that work product and IP derived from Amperesand's CI and made for the engagement vest in or are assigned to Amperesand, with a license-back to the vendor only as needed to perform.
walk_away_triggers: Any deliverables/IP-vesting clause in the NDA that assigns vendor-created work product, tooling or process improvements to the VENDOR, or grants the vendor ownership of designs derived from Amperesand's CI.
A clause deeming the vendor's tooling/fixtures (built to Amperesand's designs) the vendor's sole property with no license or transfer to Amperesand.
Capturing Amperesand's pre-existing or independently developed IP into a vendor work-for-hire / assignment construct.
A residual-tooling or 'general manufacturing know-how' carve-out that lets the vendor reuse Amperesand-specific tooling for other customers.
acceptable_fallbacks: Keeping the NDA silent on work product and expressly deferring all deliverable/IP ownership to the definitive services agreement (preferred).
A neutral placeholder acknowledging that deliverable IP will be addressed in the services agreement, with the NDA creating no ownership rights.
